headline: MP Gazi Nazrul's second wife found dead at NAM Bhaban flat
summary: Police recovered the body of 19-year-old Mariam Khatun from a flat in Dhaka's Sher-e-Bangla Nagar this evening.
details: Police recovered the body of 19-year-old Mariam Khatun, the second wife of Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam, from a flat at NAM Bhaban in Dhaka's Sher-e-Bangla Nagar.
According to Monirul Islam, officer-in-charge of Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station, Mariam's body was found hanging inside the flat.
The MP was present in the flat at the time of the recovery. Police are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident.
A Crime Scene Unit of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has been deployed to collect evidence from the scene.
On July 22, Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami expelled Gazi Nazrul Islam from the party following an internal investigation that found evidence of 'moral misconduct'.
The expulsion occurred after video clips involving the MP and a young woman circulated on social media, who was later identified by the MP and his family as his second wife.
caption:
The second wife of Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam has been found dead in a Dhaka flat.

Police recovered the body of 19-year-old Mariam Khatun, the second wife of Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam, from a flat at NAM Bhaban in Dhaka's Sher-e-Bangla Nagar.

According to Monirul Islam, officer-in-charge of Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station, Mariam's body was found hanging inside the flat.

The MP was present in the flat at the time of the recovery. Police are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident.

A Crime Scene Unit of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has been deployed to collect evidence from the scene.

On July 22, Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami expelled Gazi Nazrul Islam from the party following an internal investigation that found evidence of 'moral misconduct'.

The expulsion occurred after video clips involving the MP and a young woman circulated on social media, who was later identified by the MP and his family as his second wife.

headline_marked: BCB to launch [[new six-team franchise competition]] across three formats
headline: BCB to launch new six-team franchise competition across three formats
summary: The Bangladesh Cricket Board is overhauling domestic cricket by unifying the BCL and NCL under a corporate-owned franchise model.
details: The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) has approved a new six-team, franchise-based domestic competition that will span three formats: first-class four-day, one-day, and T20.

This overhaul unifies the Bangladesh Cricket League (BCL) and the National Cricket League (NCL) T20 under a single framework, with ownership rights offered to corporate and financial institutions for an initial three-year cycle.
The franchise era is expected to begin with the T20 tournament, which is tentatively scheduled to start in December.
The BCB also revised match fees: men's players will earn Tk 1.5 lakh for four-day, Tk 1 lakh for one-day, and Tk 80,000 for T20 matches.
Women's players will receive Tk 40,000 for three-day games, Tk 30,000 for one-day matches, and Tk 20,000 for T20s, while U-19 daily allowances have doubled to Tk 20,000.
Infrastructure upgrades were also approved, including an IAAF-approved athletic running track and new dressing rooms at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium in Dhaka.
Additionally, the board has appointed a consultant for the renovation and development of the Shaheed Chandu Stadium in Bogura.
caption:
A new era for Bangladesh cricket! The BCB is shifting to a corporate franchise model for domestic competitions.

The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) has approved a new six-team, franchise-based domestic competition that will span three formats: first-class four-day, one-day, and T20.

This overhaul unifies the Bangladesh Cricket League (BCL) and the National Cricket League (NCL) T20 under a single framework, with ownership rights offered to corporate and financial institutions for an initial three-year cycle.

The franchise era is expected to begin with the T20 tournament, which is tentatively scheduled to start in December.

The BCB also revised match fees: men's players will earn Tk 1.5 lakh for four-day, Tk 1 lakh for one-day, and Tk 80,000 for T20 matches.

Women's players will receive Tk 40,000 for three-day games, Tk 30,000 for one-day matches, and Tk 20,000 for T20s, while U-19 daily allowances have doubled to Tk 20,000.

Infrastructure upgrades were also approved, including an IAAF-approved athletic running track and new dressing rooms at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium in Dhaka.

Additionally, the board has appointed a consultant for the renovation and development of the Shaheed Chandu Stadium in Bogura.
